violations.description: The performance test measures wall-clock elapsed time and fails when the observed P95 exceeds 200 ms, so host load, scheduler contention, power state, and concurrent CI work can change the result without a code change.
violations.suggestion: Keep deterministic query-result and query-plan assertions in the test suite; move wall-clock benchmarking to a controlled benchmark job or record timings without making an ordinary test pass/fail on elapsed time.

violations.description: The Last7d assertion queries through query_intel_feed(), which reads the real system clock, while candidate() fixes published_at to 2026-08-18T08:00:00Z; the expected two results therefore expire as calendar time advances.
violations.suggestion: Inject or expose a fixed test clock/as-of instant for this integration path and assert Last7d against that fixed instant.

violations.description: The assertion identifies feed state through the styling class .feed-status, coupling synchronization to a CSS implementation detail that may change independently of behavior.
violations.suggestion: Select the state by an accessible role/name or a stable test id owned by the UI contract.

violations.description: The ordinary-stream assertion uses the styling class .feed-status as part of element discovery, making the test sensitive to presentation-only refactors.
violations.suggestion: Select the stream status through its accessible role/name or a stable test id.

violations.description: The E2E assertion waits on the styling class .feed-status, which can break on a CSS-only refactor despite unchanged user-visible behavior.
violations.suggestion: Use getByRole with an accessible name, or a stable data-testid if no appropriate semantic role exists.

violations.description: The post-switch assertion waits on the styling class .feed-status, coupling a behavioral check to mutable CSS structure.
violations.suggestion: Use a semantic status locator with an accessible name, or a stable data-testid if semantics cannot identify it uniquely.

recommendations: Inject a fixed clock/as-of instant into the Rust integration query that exercises Last7d filtering.
Separate wall-clock performance gating from deterministic functional tests and run it only in a controlled benchmark environment.
Replace all .feed-status CSS selectors with accessible role/name locators or stable test ids.
summary: The 8 direct Story 4.5 test files have 6 determinism violations: 2 HIGH wall-clock dependencies and 4 MEDIUM CSS-selector dependencies; no unseeded randomness, hard waits, unmocked external APIs, or test-order dependencies were found.
